newsitem.title: INDIA: India moves towards new coalition government.
newsitem.headline: India moves towards new coalition government.

text.p: India on Monday edged towards a resolution of its two-week political crisis, and the Congress party said a new coalition government could be in place in about a week, averting mid-term elections.

In a major concession, caretaker Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda on Sunday offered to step down as head of his 15-party United Front coalition if it would lead to a new governing agreement with Congress.
Until Sunday, Deve Gowda and his alliance partners had steadfastly refused to bow to Congress's demand that the coalition change leaders before a new government could be formed.
Deve Gowda's reversal opened the door to a possible new alignment, with Congress supporting a new governing coalition led by the United Front.
That would strongly resemble the centre-left coalition which fell last week, but deprive Hindu nationalists of a chance to strengthen their hand in snap elections.
Congress, which provoked Deve Gowda's downfall last Friday by withdrawing support for his 10-month-old government, welcomed Deve Gowda's move.
"If they (United Front) have any other leader, we are prepared to support them," Congress spokesman Vithal Gadgil told Reuters on Monday.
Asked how long it would take the United Front and Congress to work out a new deal, Gadgil said: "About a week."

The United Front was set to meet on Thursday to take up the matter of a new leader. The two political formations would have to negotiate the terms of a new power-sharing pact before the crisis could be considered over.
The rightwing Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) scoffed at its rivals' efforts to forge a new government.

"I think they are going to have another experiment," BJP spokeswoman Sushma Swaraj told Reuters. "If the first arrangement was a zero, this will also prove to be a zero. It will lower the credibility of both parties in the eyes of the nation. They are taking the electorate for a ride."
Swaraj predicted that the new United Front-led government would be short-lived because, like Deve Gowda's coalition, it would fall victim to differences with Congress.
"The new PM will have all sorts of qualities, but after six months he will be branded incompetent and a coward," she said. "There will be elections in six months."
The BJP is parliament's biggest party with 162 seats in the 542-member lower house. With its allies it controls 193 votes, ahead of the United Front's 178 and Congress's 140.
Opinion surveys show the BJP would likely be strengthened if the second general elections in a year were held now.
Asked if the BJP could be in a stronger position if polls were held in six months following more acrimony between the United Front and Congress, Swaraj said: "Yes."
The policy-making Congress Working Committee was set to meet in New Delhi at 7 p.m. (1330 GMT) on Monday.

Gadgil said Congress president Sitaram Kesri would have no difficulty satisfying a United Front demand that he withdraw a letter to President Shankar Dayal Sharma revoking Congress support for the United Front and staking a claim to power.
"He (Kesri) has already said he will not be staking a claim. There is no difficulty in withdrawing the letter," Gadgil said.
While the United Front said it was open to forming a fresh coalition under a new leader, it expressed concern over the "credibility" and "durability" of Congress' support.
"That is a matter of negotiation," Gadgil said.
Kesri had accused Deve Gowda of trying to sideline Congress.
